note: Source-evidenced classification of the Gate 0B.4 tranche. Ownership is accountability, not authorization: a classified operation names the capability responsible for it, and every gap between that operation and a kernel decision is a recorded defect with one responsible capability. Every material claim of a record cites provenance: the exact method handler, an import it uses, a service it reaches or a schema it resolves. An unresolved operation stays SCOPE_UNDECIDED with its exact evidence gap. No institutional decision recorded here is adopted, and none justifies access.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which platform staff may read across organizations or operate shared platform services, under what mandate, scope, expiry and audit?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The source uses a platform_lead role title and an isPlatformAdminUser identity check. Neither is an issued, scoped, expiring mandate. No adopted decision in the repository names a platform-staff mandate model.

institutionalDecisions.question: Does the approved per-organization representation protocol, or the kernel issuance model, decide who holds representation authority over a case?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The case-assignment engine refuses to assign without an approved protocol. The kernel also issues mandates and assignments. The source does not say which governs when they differ.

institutionalDecisions.question: Who may mark a knowledge-base row or collective agreement is_public, and what review precedes publication beyond the organization?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: AI search and summarize return another organization's row when is_public is true. Agreement creation sets isPublic false and says publication is not decided at creation. No source says who sets the flag.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which roles may read the organization audit history, and which fields must be withheld from each?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The activity feed and AI usage routes return audit-derived rows at member and administrator role floors. No adopted decision names the readers.

institutionalDecisions.question: Is observability alerting an organization-administration, platform-operations or security-monitoring obligation, and who may read its alerts?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The realtime alerts route returns an organization's alert rows at the member role floor under the grievance case suite entitlement. No capability or persona source names observability alerting.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which organization office may read the commercial terms of, pause, resume or cancel the organization platform subscription, and which of those acts belong to the platform operator?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: Subscription reads sit at the member floor, pause and resume at the steward floor, and metadata update and cancel at the secretary_treasurer role title, a union finance role. The Financial Officer disposition labels the platform billing service as not union finance. No adopted decision names the contract-authority office.

institutionalDecisions.question: Which capability and which organization office own newsletter campaigns, recipients and delivery status, and is campaign delivery status a billing or a communications obligation?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The batch-status route lives under billing and is gated by a billing entitlement but reads newsletter_campaigns and newsletter_recipients. No capability, persona source or register entry names campaigns or newsletter delivery.

institutionalDecisions.question: Does the platform operator or an organization own carbon accounting, and which measured data source, if any, may back an emissions figure or a neutrality claim?
institutionalDecisions.sourceState: The carbon routes return emissions figures written as literals in the handler, take the organization from the query string and are called by no product source; no table, service, persona source or capability record names carbon accounting.

defectRegister.title: Route name advertises a business domain but the handler is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members; GET returns member roster rows under the advertised name and every write is refused.
The super-admin role repair route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members; its documented repair does nothing and POST is refused.
The CLC organization analytics route is the generic CRUD factory over analytics_metrics, an OPERATIONAL table; any steward can create arbitrary analytics metric rows.

The mutation is audited through performAuditedOperation, which records intent and outcome in separate transactions from the effect. The manifest declares an atomic audit that the source does not show.
The route-coverage scanner misreports this operation: it marks CRUD reads as mutating, overstates the audit class, and misses the guard actually applied.
Billing history returns HTTP 200 with an empty list for a capability that has no storage; it must be an honest HTTP 501.
The target organization of a billing operation is caller-supplied and the guard checks only the caller role title, not authority over that organization.
A platform-wide read or operation is authorized by a role-title floor, not by a kernel decision or a platform-staff mandate.
Scheduled billing is latent: no scheduler calls it and the generator needs a session, so the route triggers work the system cannot run headless.
The report queries per_capita_remittances with no caller-organization predicate, so an organization administrator reads remittance data across organizations.
Administrator-only financial analytics is served with Cache-Control public, so shared caches may store it.
The organization audit log (user ids, resource ids, event details) is readable at the member role floor.
On the legacy path the AI-usage query reads audit_security rows for every organization with no organization predicate.
The organization directory returns member counts and contact name and email across organizations at a role-title floor.
PKI signing workflow state lives in a process-local Map; the signature_workflows table does not exist, so workflows are lost on restart and not shared across instances.
The representation protocol is a real, atomically audited, separation-of-duties flow that no capability names; ownership needs a Gate 0B.2 decision.
The three public-route lists disagree and the edge does not enforce them; routes that accept anonymous calls are absent from the lists.
The complete OpenAPI specification is served without authentication and is not on the public-route allowlist.
The version route exposes environment, host, deployment type, feature profile and image digests without authentication and is not on the public-route allowlist.
Tracking, click and unsubscribe handlers change state on GET (message log, campaign counters, preferences, consent records) although the manifest records them as read-only.
Anonymous telemetry is limited by a process-local in-memory limiter, which does not hold across instances.

The segment collection, segment item, segment execute and system settings routes advertise a business domain but are the generic CRUD factory over organization_members: GET returns member roster rows at the member floor, every write is refused, and nothing is segmented, executed or configured. A real member_segments table exists in the governance list and is not bound.

The update-role route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members, a READ_ONLY table: GET returns member rows at the steward floor and POST is refused, so no role change can occur through it.

The analytics routes (claims, financial, executive, heatmap, comparative, dashboard, deadlines, clause statistics, trends, insights) are the generic CRUD factory over analytics_metrics, trend_analyses or insight_recommendations, which are OPERATIONAL. GET returns stored rows, not computed analytics, and any steward can insert arbitrary rows that are then served as analytics.

The platform user directory and activity feed select organization_members and organizations with no organization predicate at a platform_lead role title and return member name, email and role across organizations. Neither read is audited.

The cross-organization analytics route selects up to 1000 analytics_metrics rows through the global db handle inside a withRLSContext call that names no organization. The source does not show which rows tenant security returns, and the route is gated by a role title.

Member deactivation and removal revoke sessions, the platform-auth membership and the local row in separate stores. The audit record is atomic only with the local status update, and the route returns 502 when a step fails, leaving a partial state for a retry.
Agreement creation reads request.json() with no schema: only the status is checked, and every other field is inserted as supplied at a steward role-title floor.

AI grievance triage, clause reasoning and the copilot read any grievance in the organization for a steward role title. They do not check that the steward holds the case, so grievance content for cases the steward does not represent is sent to a model.

Routes that run enforceAISafety with grievance_legal, confidential or pension_financial data classes call the model with dataClass internal in the service layer. The two vocabularies disagree and the source shows no mapping between them.
Finance analysis and the pension projection, funding and trustee-summary routes read dues, arrears, remittances, trial-balance and pension data for an officer role title, with no financial mandate.

The employer-risk and insight-report GET handlers insert rows (employer_risk_scores, ai_insight_reports) through the global db handle and record the invocation with a separate auditLog event that is not committed with the row.
The classify, match-precedents, summarize and search routes call a model and write no audit event in the route handler or in the service that holds the AI call.
The classify route applies no AI feature gate and no AI safety check, although every sibling AI route applies both.
AI search and summarize return another organization's knowledge row when is_public is true, and no source says who may set the flag. Public cross-tenant data is not authorized by being public.
The semantic-search status GET counts every cba_clause and arbitration_precedents row across organizations through the global db handle with no organization predicate, at the member role floor.
The AI feedback GET returns every user's rating, comment and user id for a query id in the organization at the member role floor.
The AI ingest route indexes documents into a process-local Map, so an indexed document is lost on restart and not shared across instances, while the response reports status indexed.
The embedding cache statistics GET is gated by an organization administrator role title but reports platform-wide cache state.

Signing stores signatureValue ATTESTATION over a document-reference hash. The source says there is no cryptographic signature value, so verification cannot prove who signed or that content is unchanged.

The generic CRUD create copies the whole request body into the insert and the update strips only the primary key and organization column, so a caller can set status, author, approval, cost and provenance columns on every table whose route lists no blockedPatchFields; none of the Gate 0B.3 CRUD routes lists any.

The generic CRUD delete sets status archived on any table with a status column, but the break_status, negotiation_status, proposal_status and arbitration_status enums contain no archived value, so deletion of those records cannot succeed as designed and the failure is not shown by any source.

The break collection declares ownerColumn memberId, which references organization_members.id, and the factory compares it with the session user id for every caller; the item routes hold callers below steward to the same memberId comparison. The source does not show these are the same identifier, and on the collection staff are held to the same filter so no steward can review member breaks through it.

Break creation at the member floor does not force memberId from the session because the collection route declares an explicit ownerColumn, which sets the factory low-role mode to open, so a member can record a break, with its denial and compliance fields, for another member.
The KPI configuration read returns alert thresholds and the alertRecipients column to every member at the read floor.

Disconnecting a calendar requires the fixed administrator floor of the generic delete, so a member who connected their own calendar cannot disconnect it, and the delete removes the local row holding provider tokens without revoking the provider grant.
The bulk-import route is the generic CRUD factory over organization_members, a READ_ONLY table: GET returns the member roster to staff and POST is refused, so nothing is imported.
The precedent citations, documents and search routes are the generic CRUD factory over arbitration_decisions: they return and change decision rows and serve no citations, documents or search results.

arbitration_decisions has no organization column, so the library routes return every decision row to every organization whatever isPublic or accessRestrictions say, and the row-level-security policy admits any tenant context.
The library delete uses the fixed administrator floor of the generic factory and hard-deletes the row, so an organization administrator can delete a decision that every organization reads.

A steward can insert an insight_recommendations row through the generic factory with an aiReferenceId, confidence score and recommendations of their choosing, and the row is then served as an AI insight.
The weekly summary records an AI invocation naming model analytics-engine and stores confidenceScore 0.83 and fixed recommendation text for a computation that counts events and runs no model.
The synchronized accounting invoice read returns customer names, balances and amounts to every member at the read floor, ahead of any financial mandate.
The invoice create route is the generic factory over external_invoices, a READ_ONLY table: every POST is refused, so the advertised invoice creation does not exist.
The arbitration collection and item routes read and write arbitration rows for any steward of the organization, accept any grievanceId in the body and do not check that the steward holds the case.

bargaining_proposals has no organization column, so the generic factory adds no tenant predicate to reads, updates or deletes and the create accepts any negotiationId; isolation rests only on a row-level-security policy this tranche cannot show is applied.
The batch invoicing route selects every active subscription across all organizations and generates an invoice for each at an organization administrator role title, returning every organization id.
The invoice replay route selects the invoice and its line items by id with no organization predicate at a steward role floor, so one organization can read another organization invoice.

Invoice generation, invoice replay and trial expiry declare an atomic service audit, but invoice generation records auditLog after its inserts outside a transaction, replay records a separate access event, and trial expiry writes no audit record.

The billing validation route records only application log events and labels ordinary validation failures unauthorized_access or auth_failed, so security monitoring cannot tell an attack from a wrong currency.

The observability sweep writes alert rules, executions and notifications through the module-level db handle and its audit record through the sweep transaction handle; the source shows no proof that they commit together.
The audits list presents audit-log rows as audit engagements and invents status, findings 0 and hasReport false for every row.
The audit item route returns the complete audit_logs row, with details and any recorded address and agent, to an officer role floor with no redaction by reader.

The audits routes read the audit_security audit_logs table, while persistAtomicAudit writes the domains infrastructure audit_logs table, so the routes do not show the audit records the atomic writers produce.

The bargaining-notes GET returns timeline, statistics and session-type results before the visibleToUserId confidentiality filter is applied, and the timeline returns the title of every note of an agreement whatever its confidentiality level.

The bargaining-note item GET and PATCH are the generic factory: a member reads any note by id, including restricted and confidential notes the collection route withholds, and an update skips the agreement check the collection create applies.

Tentative agreement creation verifies the parent negotiation but stores relatedProposalIds and relatedClauseId without verifying that the proposals or clause belong to that negotiation or organization.
Negotiation and tentative-agreement reads sit at the member floor and ignore confidentialityLevel, so strike-vote results, cost ceilings and costed agreements reach every member.

The trial-expiry route passes a payment-method checker that always returns false, so every expired trial of the organization is cancelled whether or not a payment method exists, at a steward role floor.
The send-invoice route generates and stores an invoice and returns it; nothing is delivered, whatever the route name advertises.

Subscription commercial terms are readable at the member floor, pause, resume, invoice generation and trial expiry sit at the steward floor, and update and cancel sit at the secretary_treasurer role title, a union finance role; no source names the office with contract authority.
calculateMetrics stores claim identifiers in the metric metadata and the metrics GET returns that metadata to every member at the member floor.

The metrics routes resolve the organization once in the route wrapper and again in the action through getOrganizationIdForUser, and the action ignores the first, so a user with more than one membership may write to an organization other than the session organization.

The derived case metrics and the weekly summary count pilot telemetry events and present them as case figures; open cases are created minus closed events and overdue cases are breached minus closed events, with no case table read.

The break compliance report returns per-member denied, missed and flagged counts to any steward while the generic break route holds a member to their own rows, so the report is authorized more broadly than the records it is computed from.

The realtime alerts route returns the raw triggerData of alert executions, with SLA-risk, ingestion-failure and payment-failure counts, to every member under a case-suite entitlement, with no redaction and no named reader.

The Google and Microsoft authorization routes pass the session user id as the OAuth state and the callbacks compare the returned state with that same id, and accept a callback with no state at all, so the state is neither unguessable nor single-use and gives no protection against a forged callback.

The provider callbacks are GET handlers that exchange a code and insert or update the connection row holding the provider tokens, and neither the callback nor the member-floor wrapper writes an audit record for the connection, so a state-changing GET leaves no audit evidence.

encryptCalendarToken returns the token unencrypted when no encryption key is configured outside production, and decryptCalendarToken returns any value without the encryption prefix as it is, so a database written without the key holds provider tokens in clear text and never fails.
The connection collection and item reads select the whole external_calendar_connections row, so the stored accessToken and refreshToken values are returned to the browser of the connection owner.

A steward can create or update a connection through the generic factory with any provider, providerAccountId, accessToken and refreshToken, stored as supplied and unencrypted, and an update can reassign userId, so the OAuth flow and the token encryption can be bypassed and a connection can be handed to another user.

The connection sync route selects the connection by id and organization only, with no userId predicate and no role above organization membership, so any member can run an import or export through another member provider account.

The sync route proves that the local calendar and event are in the organization but not that the caller owns a personal calendar or may read a personal event, so a member can import into or export from another member personal calendar.

The sync records intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around an external provider call, and the connection update runs inside that operation without the audit record; the record is not committed with the state change.

The calendar item route supplies lockedAuthCheck to reject another member personal calendar, but the factory invokes it only when beforeUpdate or mergeJsonColumns is configured and never on delete, and the route configures neither, so a steward can still update or delete another member personal calendar.

The calendar events routes filter events by calendar id and organization or by organization alone and never consult calendars.isPersonal or ownerId, which calendar_events does not carry, so a member reads events of another member personal calendar through calendars/[id]/events and staff read every personal event through calendar/events.

Event create and update store a caller-supplied calendarId without verifying that the calendar belongs to the organization or is visible to the caller; the foreign key checks only that a calendar row exists.

No table of the CBA intelligence dataset has an organization column and none of the services filters by organization, so every organization reads, and every administrator or steward writes, one shared dataset; nothing in the source states which organizations may read it or who curates it.

The agreement list, item and export reads apply a review status filter only when the caller supplies one, so extracted agreements, wage adjustments and clauses that are pending, rejected or superseded are returned as the dataset.

Source registration and update, ingestion, seeding and extraction require only an organization administrator role floor, yet they create and change the dataset every organization reads and call external services at the platform expense, so the administrator of any one organization can curate platform-wide data; no source names the platform staff mandate.

A steward of any organization can approve, reject or supersede an extracted record, which sets the review status every organization sees, and the decision records the reviewer role as the literal steward whatever the caller role is.

Extraction, ingestion runs and source seeding declare an atomic service audit, but they record intent and outcome through performAuditedOperation around many separate statements and an external provider call, so the audit record is not committed with the state change.

The benchmark GET inserts a cba_intel_benchmark_snapshots row when save=true, recording the caller user id, and the route and the service write no audit record, so a state-changing GET is both mislabelled as a read and unaudited.

The snapshot history is selected by target agreement only and returns the computedBy user id of whoever saved each snapshot, so a steward of one organization reads the user ids of stewards of other organizations.

The export route asks the service for 10000 rows but listAgreements clamps the limit to 100, so the CSV advertised as an export of the agreements holds at most the first 100 rows and says nothing about it.

Source registration accepts any URL for the base, API, feed and terms addresses, and the ingestion adapters fetch the discovered document URLs from the server with no host allow-list or private-address check, so an administrator can make the platform request internal addresses.

The moderation step returns not flagged when OPENAI_API_KEY is unset and, when the moderation request fails, returns a flagged result with the reason Safety system unavailable that sendMessage then ignores and proceeds, although the code comments call the failure closed; a member message reaches the model unmoderated whenever moderation is absent or down.

The moderation step posts the member message text directly to api.openai.com with a provider key, outside @nzila/ai-sdk which the same file names as the only route for AI calls, so the data-class, budget and audit controls of the AI control plane do not apply to that call.

The message route marks every reply reviewRequired false and passes the literal role member to enforceAISafety whatever the caller role is, although the service describes the output as advisory with human stewardship preserved, so the policy check never sees the caller real role and the response never asks for review.

When the model call fails the service stores a fixed apology as an assistant message with model fallback, and the route returns it as a successful response marked aiGenerated true with the configured deployment name as the model, so an outage is persisted in the transcript and reported as a model reply.

Retrieval selects at most three active knowledge rows of the organization with no ordering and no vector predicate and only then scores them by similarity, so the context sent to the model is an arbitrary subset of the knowledge base rather than the most relevant documents.

The session list and the message read apply no status condition, so archived and deleted sessions stay listed and readable, and the message read applies neither the ai_chatbot entitlement, the AI feature flag, the AI safety check nor a rate limit, so a transcript stays readable after the feature is disabled.

The list, item, tags, compare and search reads run on the system role, which bypasses row-level security, and the only boundary between organizations is a hand-written application predicate; the route comments name this PRIVILEGED_CROSS_TENANT_REVIEW and no kernel decision stands behind it.

The item authority canReadSharedClause admits a federation clause only when the nearest federation ancestor of the caller equals that of the owner, while the list and search predicate admits it whenever the caller federation appears anywhere in the owner hierarchy path, so when federations nest the list and search return clauses the item, tags and compare reads refuse.

The item read returns originalEmployerName and the creator user id to any reader whatever isAnonymized says, and every read returns the owning organization name, so a clause shared as anonymized discloses the employer it was anonymized from.

The item read returns the createdBy user id of the clause, and the tags read returns whole clause_library_tags rows with their createdBy user id, to stewards of other organizations that may read the clause.

A steward of any organization can create or change a clause to sharing level public, which exposes its text to every organization; sharingChangeDenial checks only federation and congress eligibility, and no source names who may publish collective-agreement text.

Clause create, update, sharing update and tag writes store clause text, title, type, dates, anonymization fields and tag names from the body with no schema validation; only sharingLevel and sharedWithOrgIds are checked, so a malformed value reaches the database or throws as an unhandled error.

Clause create stores a caller-supplied originalClauseId that the schema notes as a foreign key to cba_clauses that is not enforced, and the route checks sourceCbaId against the organization but never checks originalClauseId, so a clause can point at another organization clause.

The update overwrites the shared clause text and sharing fields without raising version or setting previousVersionId, and the delete removes the row and its tags permanently, so organizations that compared or cited a clause see it change silently or vanish, and only the audit record remains.

The compare POST increments comparisonCount on rows owned by other organizations under the system role, and the audit record it commits belongs to the comparing organization, so a reader changes data it does not own and the owner has no record of it.

The compare GET returns a usage message with status 200 and performs no comparison, and the compare POST returns commonKeywords as the constant empty list, so part of the advertised analysis is a placeholder presented as a result.

The clc dashboard, remittances and sync routes are the same generic CRUD configuration over clc_sync_log, and no other code in the application reads or writes that table, so the dashboard and remittance routes return and create synchronization log rows and serve no dashboard or remittance, and the sync route records a log entry and starts no synchronization.

The routes read the whole clc_sync_log row, with errorMessage, errorDetails, syncData and dataHash, at the member floor, and the steward create stores any body field, including status, record counts, isVerified, verifiedBy and verifiedAt, so a steward can record a synchronization as verified that never ran and every member can read integration error details.

The CNESST filing collection declares ownerColumn memberId, so the factory compares the uuid memberId column with the session user id for every caller, steward included, while the item routes declare no ownerColumn and let a steward read any filing of the organization; the source does not show that the session user id is the member id, so the collection and the item routes disagree about which filings a steward may see.

The CNESST filing item routes and the create read and write any filing of the organization for a steward role floor, accept any memberId, incidentId and unionRepId in the body, and do not check that the steward represents the member the filing concerns; a filing holds the member injury narrative, outcome and compensation awarded.

anti_scab_violations has no createdBy column, so the factory records no author, reportedById and reportedByName are taken from the body rather than the session, and any steward of the organization can change the outcome fields (resolved, penaltyAmount, injunctionGranted, tatFileNumber) of any violation record.

The anti-scab violation and joint committee tables have no status column, so the fixed administrator delete of the factory removes the regulatory record permanently; only the audit record of the delete remains, and no source names a retention rule for them.

The joint committee read sits at the member floor and returns the worker representative list with member identifiers, names and roles, and the worker co-chair identifier, to every member of the organization.

The agreement detail GET increments collective_agreements.view_count in a tenant transaction whenever includeAnalytics=true, at the member floor, with no audit record, so a read-only operation changes stored state and any member can inflate the counter.

The agreement detail returns clauses and bargaining notes by cbaId alone: getClausesByCBAId and getBargainingNotesByCBA carry no organization predicate, and the clause create stores any cbaId, so a clause written by one organization against another organization agreement id is returned in that agreement detail.

The clause create is the generic factory, which stores the body cbaId, a foreign key to collective_agreements.id that no organization condition guards, so a steward can attach clauses to the agreement of another organization; the organization column is forced from the session but the agreement is not checked.
The clause item GET passes countView true on every request that does not ask for the hierarchy, so each read updates cba_clauses.view_count at the member floor with no audit record.
The clause search route is the generic CRUD configuration over cba_clauses and applies no search term: GET lists clause rows and POST creates a clause, so no search is performed.

The clause comparison groups clauses by type, always returns empty differences and best practices, and returns three fixed recommendation sentences whatever the clauses say; the route returns this as an analysis and, with save true, stores it as the analysis result of a named comparison.
The agreement list passes the caller limit and page, parsed without a ceiling, to the service, which clamps neither, so a member can request an unbounded page of agreements.

With includeNotes=true the agreement detail returns every bargaining note of the agreement whose confidentiality level is public or internal to any member at the member floor, so internal bargaining notes reach members who hold no bargaining role.

collective_agreements.cba_number carries a single unique constraint across every organization, and the create and update routes answer a duplicate with a conflict, so a steward of one organization learns whether any organization holds a given agreement number and cannot use a number another organization holds.

The newsletter delivery status route is gated by the financial_intelligence_suite entitlement, a finance product gate, so the entitlement that decides who may read campaign delivery state is unrelated to the data and to the communications obligation.

Any job id that does not start with campaign-, and any campaign id that is not found, returns status processing with zero counts and a start time of the moment of the request, so a job that does not exist is reported as running.
The status response lists the e-mail address of up to ten failed recipients to any steward holding the entitlement and records no audit of the disclosure.

Case studies are global marketing rows read by every organization and the public, yet create, update and delete sit at the organization admin role floor, so the admin of any one organization can publish, rewrite or remove content shown to all organizations; no source names the platform staff mandate that should hold this write.

The public case-study list and the member item read filter on neither visibility nor publishedAt, and the list status filter reads a status column that case_studies does not have, so unpublished rows and rows marked authenticated are returned to anonymous callers and to members of every organization.

The carbon dashboard and infrastructure routes return emissions totals, regional breakdowns, renewable percentages and optimization advice as literals in the handler, with success true and status 200, for any authenticated caller, so invented measurements are presented as monitoring results.
The carbon dashboard takes organizationId from the query string, defaults it to union-eyes and echoes it, so the response names an organization chosen by the caller and not the session organization.

The carbon validation route computes a certificationEligible result and a message of Eligible for certification from numbers the caller supplied, with no source for the data points and no record of the check, so an unverified figure yields a certification-shaped answer.

operations.persona: Steward holding the financial_intelligence_suite entitlement
operations.authorizationDetail: withRoleAuth('steward') plus requireEntitlement financial_intelligence_suite, a finance product entitlement that has no relation to newsletters. A role title is not a kernel decision.
operations.tenantScope: The campaign lookup filters newsletter_campaigns on the session organizationId; the recipient statistics filter only on the campaign id taken from that lookup.
operations.dataOwnership: newsletter_campaigns and newsletter_recipients rows of the organization; no route or service in the source writes either table.
operations.dataSensitivity: Recipient e-mail addresses of failed deliveries and campaign delivery counts
operations.privacyDisclosure: Up to ten failed recipient e-mail addresses with their error text are returned to a steward.
operations.auditDetail: A read of campaign delivery state; nothing is written, and the disclosure of recipient addresses is not audited.
operations.requiredAudit: Audit reads of recipient e-mail addresses once the communications capability that owns the route is named.
operations.implementedBehavior: Returns delivery progress for a job id that starts with campaign-; any other job id, and a campaign that is not found, returns status processing with zero counts and a start time of now.
operations.requiredFutureGuard: Move the route under the communications capability, gate it by a communications entitlement, return not found for an unknown job, and audit reads of recipient addresses.
operations.callerFinding: No caller outside the API tree, tests, documentation and capability registries names this route path in tracked product source.

operations.persona: Organization member or above through the generic CRUD factory
operations.authenticationMechanism: Authenticated session resolved by the generic CRUD factory (crudRoutes over withApi).
operations.authorizationDetail: Generic CRUD role floor: GET requires member, with every row held to userId equal to the session user id. A role title is not a kernel decision.
operations.tenantScope: orgScoped: true and the table has an organization column: the factory scopes the query to the session organization.
operations.dataOwnership: external_calendar_connections rows owned by one user within one organization; they hold provider access and refresh tokens.
operations.dataSensitivity: Calendar provider connection with access token, refresh token, provider account and provider e-mail
operations.privacyDisclosure: The whole row, including the accessToken and refreshToken columns, is returned in the response to the connection owner.
operations.auditDetail: A read: the generic factory writes no row and no audit record.
operations.requiredAudit: Reads need no audit record unless the rows carry personal data; then audit them once the readers are named.
operations.implementedBehavior: Returns the caller own external_calendar_connections rows (ownerColumn userId), complete with token columns, at a role floor of member.
operations.requiredFutureGuard: Create and change connections only through the audited OAuth flow, never return token columns, encrypt tokens under a required key, and let a member at the member floor manage only their own connection.
operations.callerFinding: 1 call site(s) in product source name this route path; the search is route-level and does not determine the HTTP method each site uses.

operations.persona: Organization steward or above through the generic CRUD factory
operations.authenticationMechanism: Authenticated session resolved by the generic CRUD factory (crudRoutes over withApi).
operations.authorizationDetail: Generic CRUD role floor: PATCH requires steward, with every row held to userId equal to the session user id. A role title is not a kernel decision.
operations.tenantScope: orgScoped: true and the table has an organization column: the factory scopes the query to the session organization.
operations.dataOwnership: external_calendar_connections rows owned by one user within one organization; they hold provider access and refresh tokens.
operations.dataSensitivity: Calendar provider connection with access token, refresh token, provider account and provider e-mail
